game: صانع التاريخ (Sanei Al-Tarikh): grand strategy, player leads one nation on a world map. Rebuild from zero; keep only the idea.
userConditions: Lightness: never heavy on the iPhone (smooth map, low memory, low battery and heat, fast start).
Realism: realistic simulation and real-world data.
Strong foundation: the base must hold for the future so we never go back to fix or rebuild it.

decisions.install: user has a signing certificate; GitHub Actions builds an unsigned IPA; user signs and installs; user has no Mac
decisions.time: real-time with pause and speed levels, daily tick
decisions.map: countries divided into provinces; our own curated province layer (~2,500-3,000) built from Natural Earth admin-1 with stable IDs; owner vs controller per province
decisions.publishing: may be sold: only commercially licensable data and assets; license registry per data source; CI rejects non-commercial/share-alike sources; generated attribution screen

scenarios.rule: each scenario is data only; no code changes to add one

decisions.endDate: 2100 (realistic data/tech to ~2050 from published projections, studied projections 2050-2100; UN WPP projections to 2100 for population calibration; IPCC climate scenarios)
decisions.economy: detailed markets and goods from the start: ~20 goods, province industries with inputs/outputs, 3 labour skill tiers, national markets with monthly price clearing, world market with transport/tariff friction, trade blocs and sanctions, top-10 trading partners per country (no full bilateral matrix)
decisions.politics: detailed parties and elections from the start: real 2011 parties in all countries with elections (~120), top 3-6 parties each + 'others', support per province seeded from last real election, real election calendar, coalitions, interest groups backing parties; non-democracies have ruling party/factions and emergent opposition
decisions.leaders: real names, no photos, neutral text
decisions.presets: realistic default; presets (strong, superpower, god) and cheats optional and clearly labelled on setup screen
decisions.military: automated fronts only (player assigns armies to fronts and gives hold/attack orders with target arrows; same operational AI runs player and AI fronts); generic equipment generations (no real weapon names); simplified air (air superiority per region) and naval (fleets per sea zone with missions) in v1, base ready for detail later; equipment strength modelled from 20-year defence spending, personnel and tech tier, shown as estimates
decisions.nuclear: deterrence; use that reaches top escalation rung ends the game with a sober text screen
decisions.events: conditional historical events + generic events + player decisions
decisions.espionage: full from the start: agency budget/level, agent networks per country, intel gathering, counter-intelligence, sabotage, cyber, tech theft, support opposition/insurgents, election/media influence, coup support; exposure risk with diplomatic fallout. NO assassinations.
decisions.disputedTerritories: show de facto control with dashed borders for disputed areas + toggle for de jure (international legal) view; neutral labels
decisions.visualStyle: modern command room, comfortable for the eyes, strong sense of control and command (calm low-glare palette, not pure black, no harsh neon)
decisions.sound: UI sounds + haptics in v1; licensed music later
decisions.saves: autosave each in-game month rotating 3 slots + on background + unlimited named manual saves + export/import via Files (default, user did not object yet)
decisions.language: Arabic only in v1, RTL, localization-ready for English later (default)
decisions.repository: D-1: new PUBLIC repository (user's choice; free standard CI runners; code visible to everyone)
decisions.autosaveCadence: D-4: each in-game month, at most once per 2 real minutes
decisions.maxSpeed: D-16: 30 in-game days per second (2011 to 2100 in about 18 min)
decisions.godPresetName: D-12: the preset keeps the English name 'God'. On 2026-10-20 the owner first chose «حكم مطلق», then approved the original settings page with 'God', knowing this reverses that choice
decisions.electionLoss: D-9: player plays on in OPPOSITION after losing an election until returning to power (+3-4 weeks; needs opposition gameplay and its screens)
decisions.disputed2011: D-8: as in reality on 1 Jan 2011 (PA playable; Gaza Hamas-led de facto government inside polity pse; East Jerusalem and Golan 'annexation not recognised'; Western Sahara split at the berm; limited-recognition label)
decisions.rivalGovernments: D-29: any government administering a province at start is playable via a small chooser (UN-seat holder default); chooser needs a design approval
decisions.saveLocation: D-28: Documents (visible in Files) + optional automatic mirror folder chosen once (e.g. iCloud Drive)
decisions.testDevices: D-21: no XR loan possible. Replace with: (a) an 'XR budget mode' in debug builds on the user's iPhone 17 Pro Max (memory cap 160 MB, tile cache 16 MB, 60 Hz cap, XR texture limits) with time budgets tightened by the A12-to-A19 Pro speed gap (roughly 3-4x, to measure); (b) deterministic work counters on Linux CI; (c) iOS Simulator XR layout and UI tests on GitHub macOS runners. Residual risk accepted: real heat, GPU and battery on an A12 are not measured.
decisions.moneyDisplay: D-6: nominal current USD; «لماذا؟» also shows constant 2011 USD
decisions.protestImages: keep both: Arab city for Arab countries, European city for the rest
decisions.menuBackground: user will send a larger version (>= 2868x1320, same composition)
decisions.imageGenerator: all game images made by the owner with ChatGPT (OpenAI) on a paid plan; terms to re-check before release
decisions.publicPersonalDetails: owner keeps phone model, no-Mac and sideload-with-signing-certificate details public
decisions.oldGameMentions: remove mentions of the old game's failures from public documents (done 2026-10-20)
decisions.screen3NewGame: APPROVED 2026-10-20: the three pages exactly as the owner first chose them on iPhone 17 Pro Max (p1A, p2B, p3B; pixel-identical), fitted to all 7 iPhones. The cross-page header unification was declined, so page 1 keeps its plain-text back button
decisions.D-18: historical events mode: flexible (events fire only when their conditions hold; player choices can change history)
decisions.D-22: event volume v1: 80 historical, 50 generic, 40 decisions
decisions.D-14: historical targeted killings: neutral news only
decisions.D-30: no personality traits written or shown for real leaders; generated future leaders may have traits
decisions.D-19: fog of war: estimates that sharpen with intelligence; no reveal-all toggle
decisions.D-20: climate impacts on by default, can be switched off in campaign settings
decisions.D-24: the campaign ends on 31 Dec 2100 with an end screen
decisions.D-15: unit movement: smooth and realistic but light, like the owner's reference game (General / World War style); not discrete jumps. Budget rules: animate only on-screen moving units, render frames only while something moves, simplify at maximum speed or when the phone is hot. Needs a moving prototype approved by the owner (with the military fronts screen)
decisions.D-10: party data: tier A about 40 countries by province, tier B about 80 modelled from national results (<=12 parties each)
decisions.D-11: about 10 releasable states, created by events or negotiation only; insurgent states can also form at runtime
decisions.D-13: generic intelligence agency names (no real agency names)
decisions.D-27: starting equipment = 20-year defence spending + legacy stock that existed in 1991 + arms imports, as a carry-forward pool
decisions.D-7: month names يناير… by default, with a setting for كانون الثاني…
decisions.D-17: logo font: a free commercially licensed (OFL) Arabic font; owner picks from 3 samples
decisions.D-5: maximum zoom about 1.0 km/pt so small areas (Lebanon, West Bank, Bahrain) are easy to tap; final after the map test on the owner's phone
decisions.D-23: historical packs (1990, 1985, 1979) reuse the same 2004 NASA imagery; borders change by year
decisions.D-2: imagery quality medium (z7, about 20-36 MB of the app); final after the device test
decisions.D-2b: map labels drawn with the light method (glyph distance-field atlas); switch only if small Arabic looks soft on the device
decisions.D-3: OPAQUE panels always, no blur (owner's choice for lightness). Changes the approved glass look of screens 1-3: show the owner the opaque look before applying it
decisions.D-26: imagery: NASA Blue Marble NG with topography and bathymetry (real satellite imagery; equally light on the phone as our own bake). Chosen from the owner's criteria (light + realistic). AI-generated map declined: cannot match real coastlines and borders. Pending: bathymetry licence check, and the owner's approval of the look on the device
decisions.D-25: schedule: EARLY VERSION first. A playable v0.5 after M3 (map, economy, politics, events; no military yet), then M4-M8. Same total of about 95-125 weeks, re-estimated after M0b and M1a; cut content before foundation; anything touching an owner decision goes back to the owner
